# Synthetic data card — ParchiMatch Lite

**Everything in this folder is synthetic.** No real shop, customer, order or shopkeeper is behind it. It was generated by [`tools/gen-synthetic.ts`](../../tools/gen-synthetic.ts) with seed `2026`, so anyone can regenerate the seeded data files and their hashes byte for byte. The lock's `created` timestamp records the run time and will differ between runs.

## What's here

| File | What | Count |
|---|---|---|
| `catalog.csv` | An imaginary FMCG wholesaler's item list, in the format a billing export would be converted to | 111 SKUs, 61 product families |
| `dev.jsonl` | Labelled order lines for tuning, aliases, prompts and (optionally) fine-tuning seeds | 320 |
| `test.jsonl` | Labelled held-out order lines. **Locked** (`test.jsonl.lock.json`, sha256) before any model saw them | 80 (29 need review) |
| `orders/order-*.txt` | WhatsApp-style full orders with greetings and comma-joined items, for the demo (unlabelled) | 8 |
| `stats.json` | Tag and status counts for dev and test | |

## How lines are generated

For each line the generator picks a real-looking SKU, then decides how a customer would write it:

- **Name:** catalogue alias, Hindi/Hinglish name (`tata namak`, `amul makhan`, `fortune tel`), pack colour (`lays nila`), brand-only (`cadbury`, `dettol`), or Devanagari (`पारले जी`).
- **Misspelling** (30%): one edit, such as a dropped vowel, doubled letter, swapped letters or a sound-alike swap (`oo→u`, `v→w`, `c→k`).
- **Variant:** a price (`5/-`, `10 wala`, `rs 20`, `₹10`, `10 ka`) or pack size (`1kg`, `500 gm`, `1 ltr`, `adha kg`, `75 grm`), more often when it's needed to tell variants apart.
- **Quantity and unit:** Hinglish unit words (`petti`, `darjan`, `nag`, `bora`), Hindi numbers (`do petti`), glued (`2ctn`), unit-first (`ctn 2`), quantity-first word order, and fillers (`bhej do`).
- **Deliberate problems:** items the shop doesn't stock (some containing a stocked name: `tata salt lite`, `surf excel matic`, `maggi atta noodles`), a price/size the shop doesn't carry, missing quantity, missing unit, unknown unit words (`ladi`, `jodi`, `tray`), and cartons of items with no known carton size.

**Gold labels** come from what the generator intended, read the way a careful shopkeeper would: if the written words fit more than one SKU, gold is `needs_review` with no SKU. Quantity and unit are recorded as ordered (`2 carton`), not converted.

**Shop conventions baked in:** plain "maggi" means the single pack, and "surf" means Surf Excel Easy Wash. A real shop may differ.

## Process followed (to keep the test honest)

1. Generated **practice data only** in a scratch folder and ran exact and fuzzy matching on it to look for wrong gold labels. None were found among the dangerous rows; one real parser bug was found (unknown unit words were dropped) and fixed against practice data.
2. Generated the final set. The **test lines come from a separate seed** (2027), and practice lines that copy or nearly copy a test line (trigram similarity ≥ 0.85) were rejected. `npm run check-leak` confirms none remain.
3. Locked `test.jsonl` with its hash. The harness refuses to score it if it changes.
4. Ran every method **once** on the locked test. Any later change to the system must be justified on `dev.jsonl` only.

## Limitations

- **The noise model is my guess at how shopkeepers write.** Real orders will contain things this generator never produces: voice-note transcripts, totals, payment chatter, regional languages beyond Hindi, shop-specific nicknames, and multiple items per line.
- **The same author wrote the generator and the system.** The test is held out from the system, but not from the author's assumptions. Treat results as "works on the kinds of shorthand I thought of".
- **Catalogue values are illustrative.** MRPs, carton sizes and pack-colour nicknames are plausible but not verified against any company's current products or prices. Brand names are used only as product names in a fictional catalogue.
- **Proportions are arbitrary.** For example, about a third of lines need review; a real shop's rate is unknown.

## How to describe this honestly in the DEV post

Suggested wording:

> I don't have access to a wholesaler yet, so I built a **synthetic benchmark**: a 111-item FMCG catalogue and 400 order lines generated with a seeded noise model (Hinglish names, misspellings, `petti`/`darjan`, `5 wala`, Devanagari, items the shop doesn't stock). I locked 80 lines as a test set before running any model on them. The generator is in the repo, so you can reproduce or extend it.

Don't present these lines as real orders, and don't invent a shopkeeper or first-user feedback.

## A cheap upgrade: a human-written test set

The single best improvement, and doable in an hour without a shop:

1. Send 3–5 friends or relatives a screenshot of 15 catalogue items.
2. Ask: "Type this as a WhatsApp order to your kirana supplier, the way you'd really write it." Don't show them any examples.
3. Label their lines with `gold` answers (the harness format above), save as `data/human/test.jsonl`, lock it with `npm run split` (or write the lock directly), and run the harness once.

That gives a test the generator's author did not write. Credit the contributors (with permission) in the post.
